title: Tor for complementary regular local quotients
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a regular local ring with residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $r,s\geq0$ be integers with $\dim A=r+s$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $I,J\subsetneq A$ be ideals such that $A/I$ and $A/J$ are regular local rings, $\dim(A/I)=s$, $\dim(A/J)=r$, and $I+J=\mathfrak m$. There exists a regular system of parameters $f_1,\ldots,f_{r+s}$ for $A$ with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ such that $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ is an $A$-regular sequence and its images form an $A/J$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The quotient augmentation of the finite free Koszul complex $K_\bullet(A,f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] is a resolution of $A/I$; after tensoring with $A/J$ its homology is zero in positive degrees and is canonically $A/(I+J)=\kappa$ in degree zero. Consequently, as $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules],
$$\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(A/I,A/J)=0\ (i>0),\qquad \operatorname{Tor}^A_0(A/I,A/J)\simeq\kappa.$$
In particular the alternating sum of their $A$-module lengths is $1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. The statement includes $r=0$ or $s=0$, with the empty Koszul sequence interpreted in degree zero. Here an ideal of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup stable under multiplication by elements of $R$; $(S)$ denotes the ideal of finite sums of ring multiples of elements of $S$, and $R/L$ is the quotient by $u\sim v\iff u-v\in L$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to $A,I$, which are regular local and a proper ideal with regular local quotient. Obtain parameters $f_1,\ldots,f_d$, $d=r+s$, and $0\leq c\leq d$ with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $\dim(A/I)=d-c$. Thus $s=r+s-c$, so $c=r$. The same node makes the full parameter list regular. Its first $r$ entries are regular by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: the required successive injectivities are the first $r$ of those for the full list, and the prefix quotient is nonzero since it surjects onto the nonzero final quotient. This gives the required parameters, ideal equality and $A$-regularity.

proof.text: Put $B=A/J$ and write $\bar f_i$ for the image of $f_i$ in $B$. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the unique maximal ideal of $B$ is $\mathfrak m/J$: maximal ideals of the quotient correspond by inverse image to maximal ideals of $A$ containing $J$. Since $I+J=\mathfrak m$ and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, it is generated by $\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_r$. As $B$ is regular local of dimension $r$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] says these $r$ generators are a $B$-regular sequence. This argument also applies when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B1I, intersection-lemma-transversal, proof: regular parameters and the Koszul calculation; algebra.tex, Tags 00NR and 00NQ; more-algebra.tex, Tag 062F.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] with $R=M=A$, the complex $K_\bullet(A,f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ has zero positive homology. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], it is a finite free complex, $K_0=A$, and $d_1(e_i)=f_i$; thus $\operatorname{im}d_1=I$ and $H_0=A/I$. The quotient map $K_0=A\to A/I$ therefore supplies the claimed resolution, with the stated quotient augmentation.

source.place: Tag 0B1I, intersection-lemma-transversal, proof: regular parameters and the Koszul calculation; algebra.tex, Tags 00NR and 00NQ; more-algebra.tex, Tag 062F.

proof.text: The $B$-regular sequence of step 2 is also $A$-regular on the $A$-module $B$: at each index its successive quotient is the identical group $B/(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_{i-1})B$, and multiplication by $f_i$ is multiplication by $\bar f_i$. This verifies the injectivity hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] for $R=A$, $M=B$, giving $H_i(K_\bullet(A,f)\otimes_A B)=0$ for $i>0$. By the degree-zero and degree-one basis and differential formulas of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], the last differential has image $IB$ in $K_0\otimes_A B=B$, so $H_0=B/IB$. Its canonical identification with $A/(I+J)=\kappa$ sends the class of $a+J$ to $a+(I+J)$: it is onto, and its kernel before taking the quotient is precisely $IB=(I+J)/J$.

source.place: Tag 0B1I, intersection-lemma-transversal, proof: regular parameters and the Koszul calculation; algebra.tex, Tags 00NR and 00NQ; more-algebra.tex, Tag 062F.

proof.text: Compute Tor from the free resolution in step 3, using [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Step 4 gives the asserted positive-degree vanishing and the canonical degree-zero isomorphism with $\kappa$. Every $A$-submodule of $\kappa$ is a $\kappa$-vector subspace, since the $A$-action surjects onto the residue field; a nonzero element generates its one-dimensional space. Hence its only submodules are $0$ and $\kappa$, so [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives length one; the zero higher modules have length zero. Their alternating length sum is therefore $1$. All steps allow zero-length lists: if $r=0$, $I=0$, $J=\mathfrak m$ and the Koszul complex is $A[0]$; if $s=0$, the chosen prefix is the full parameter list, so $I=\mathfrak m$ and $A/I=\kappa$. No positive-dimension assumption was used.

It creates no new nodes. The item statement is byte-identical to the statement from the Q134 split, and stmt_deps gains only def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters, which the statement uses. I checked it against Stacks 0B1I (intersection.tex, lemma-transversal, line 796): the proof follows its parameter, Koszul and Tor route. Step 1: 00NR applied to (A,I), and the 00NQ prefix dimension gives c=r. The prefix is regular because its injectivities are the first r of the full list's and A/(f_1..f_r) surjects onto κ≠0. Step 2: m/J is generated by the images of f_1..f_r because I+J=m, so by 00NQ they form a B-regular sequence; r=0 also holds. Step 3: 062F with R=M=A, and K_0=A with d_1(e_i)=f_i, give a resolution of A/I. Step 4: the module form of 062F with R=A, M=A/J only needs injectivity, which holds; H_0=B/IB≅A/(I+J)=κ. Step 5 (elementary): Tor comes from the resolution by definition, and κ has length 1. Edge cases checked: k[[x,y]] with I=(x), J=(y); r=0 (J=m); s=0 (I=m, J=0 since A is a domain); and the non-transverse case I=J=(x), which the hypothesis excludes. A search of the DAG found no duplicate. The three sk-thm-p1 algebra nodes declared in split_report.tool_uses are accepted as generic tools; the unit route is kept. No SGA source is used.
